tools.name: SuggestPluginInstall
tools.description:
Render an inline card of plugins the user can add to claude.ai, taken from SearchPlugins results. The card handles all install UI; do not describe the plugins in text.

Offer one when the task is the kind a plugin could take over or make repeatable (deploys, reviews against a team process, or the ticket, data and document workflows a user's org may have packaged as plugins) and nothing enabled covers it; the user does not need to ask about plugins. Also when they ask for plugin recommendations. First call SearchPlugins with keywords drawn from the task, then pass the relevant results here: pluginId from each result's id, pluginName from its name, description as returned. Set trigger ('proactive' when you initiated this from task context, 'user_asked' when they asked). Use ListPlugins for plugins they already have.

After the card, continue the task. Example: "ship this to staging" and a deploy plugin that is not enabled → contextLabel "For your deploys".

Do NOT call this for one-off questions you can answer directly, when you are unsure a plugin would help, when SearchPlugins returned nothing relevant (then continue the task without mentioning the search), or if you already rendered a plugin or skill suggestion this conversation and the user didn't engage.

tools.name: ToolSearch
tools.description:
Fetches full schema definitions for deferred tools so they can be called.

Deferred tools appear by name in <system-reminder> messages. Until fetched, only the name is known — there is no parameter schema, so the tool cannot be invoked. This tool takes a query, matches it against the deferred tool list, and returns the matched tools' complete JSONSchema definitions inside a <functions> block. tools.name: mcp__ccd_turn__update_plan
tools.description:
Keep the task list the app shows under your latest message while you work. Every request that edits files or runs more than one command gets one (implement-and-test, investigate-then-fix, anything the user listed); only a single-command answer or pure conversation does not.

Never spend a message on this tool alone: send it IN THE SAME MESSAGE as another tool call (in parallel), so it costs no extra round trip.
- First call: with the VERY FIRST tool call of the turn, even one that only reads or lists files: {"items": [...]}, the whole plan in order, short imperative phrases (at most ~7 words, no numbering), the step you are starting "in_progress", the rest "pending". If you must look around first, make "Look at how X is set up" step one and refine the list once you know.
- Next step: {"advance": true} alongside the call that begins it (completes the in_progress step, starts the next pending one); after the last step, advance alongside wrap_up.
- Out of order: {"done": [2], "start": 4} (1-based).
- Plan changed, including right after the user interrupts or sends a new instruction mid-task: {"items": [...]} again, the new whole list, so the pinned list never shows an abandoned plan.
- Every {"items"} call says in "scope" what this request is to the session: "first_task" (nothing finished here yet); after that, "new_task" (unrelated work: it builds on nothing done, found or decided here) or "continuation" (everything else: anything a few tool calls settle, the next iteration, acting on what you just investigated or suggested, even if that work gets its own commit or PR; when unsure, this one). A "new_task" turn opens with a start_session offer and reaches this call only if the user chose Do it here.
Keep exactly one step in_progress while working and none when everything is done. Do not also write the plan as a numbered list in your message: the pinned list is the plan.

tools.name: mcp__ccd_turn__wrap_up
tools.description:
Fill the "next step" box the app shows at the end of your turn: a two-or-three-sentence recap and, when this turn leaves the user a decision to make or a step to take, one question and buttons that answer it; a turn with nothing pending ends with the recap alone, and the app then draws no box. Call it once in EVERY turn in which you kept a task list, changed files, ran commands, or completed multi-step work: when this turn's work is done, before any closing message (it also checks off the task list; no closing update_plan is needed). Skip it for short answers, pure conversation, or a brief read-and-explain turn — a reply that names a follow-up is not brief: ask or propose it, and call this.

Your closing message is ordinary text right after this call, the last thing you say this turn: your answer to the user in full, which the recap never replaces. Never write it before this call, where it can reach the user cut to a short summary. The result says whether the box shows your question: ask in the message only a question it does not show.

Fields — recap and ask are said to the user, in the second person; a reply button's label is the user's words back to you:
- recap: what is now true or changed, then where it stands, including what is not done or not verified (for example: nothing committed, or not checked in the app). Two or three short sentences, about 40 words / 300 characters, in the project's own words. No recommendation here.
- ask (with actions, only when the next move is the user's call — a choice of approach, a go-ahead to fix, commit, push, post or send, an approval): just that ONE decision in one short sentence, never two joined by "and" ("Which fix first?"), with no reason or recommendation and without listing the options the buttons give: your pick, actions[0], is drawn as the primary button. At most 100 characters.
Every field is a top-level parameter holding plain prose (actions: a JSON array); none contains markup or another field.

recap.description: Two or three short sentences to the user (≤300 chars): what is now true or changed, then where it stands, including what is not done or not verified. Its first sentence is the sidebar status. It must stand on its own, since it is also read away from the transcript and the box draws under anything you write after this call: never point at anything else in the conversation ("listed below", "see above", "in my message").

blocked.description: true when your work stops here until the user answers (the app marks the session as waiting on them); omit when the answer can wait.

action.description: An app action update_plan's result listed as available now, or one your own work this turn made available; anything else is refused, and one that stops being available later is dropped (as actions[0], with your ask and the other answers), so do not guess. Omit for a reply.

tools.name: mcp__Claude_Browser__browser_batch
tools.description: Execute a sequence of Browser pane tool calls in ONE round trip. Each item is {name, input} where input is exactly what you'd pass to that tool standalone. Actions execute SEQUENTIALLY (not in parallel) and stop on the first error. Use this tool extensively to quickly execute work whenever you can predict two or more steps ahead — e.g. navigate, click a field, type, press Return, screenshot. Each tool's own permission check runs per item — a step on a site the user hasn't allowed either asks the user inline (and continues if they allow) or is refused, which stops the batch; if a step is refused for a missing permission, call that tool on its own (that call can ask the user), then batch the rest. Screenshots and other images are returned interleaved with outputs; coordinates you write in THIS batch refer to the screenshot taken BEFORE this call. browser_batch cannot be nested, and preview_start is not batchable — but if the Browser pane isn't open yet, a batch whose FIRST action is navigate with a url opens it (other actions still need an open page).

input.description: That tool's input — same shape you'd pass when calling it directly. For computer items whose action is left_click, right_click, double_click, triple_click, left_click_drag, key or type, and for form_input items, include action_summary in the item's input, as you would when calling that tool directly.

tools.name: mcp__Claude_Browser__computer
tools.description: Mouse/keyboard automation in the Browser pane. Clicks accept either `coordinate` (pixels in the coordinate frame of the most recent `computer{action:"screenshot"}` — reported with every scaled screenshot; equal to the image's pixels for unscaled ones) or `ref` (a `ref_N` from read_page/find). Whenever you intend to click on an element like an icon, you should consult a screenshot to determine the coordinates of the element first; after the tab loads a different site, take a new screenshot before clicking by `coordinate`.

schema.name: mcp__Claude_Browser__computer
schema.description: Mouse/keyboard automation in the Browser pane. Clicks accept either `coordinate` (pixels in the coordinate frame of the most recent `computer{action:"screenshot"}` — reported with every scaled screenshot; equal to the image's pixels for unscaled ones) or `ref` (a `ref_N` from read_page/find). Whenever you intend to click on an element like an icon, you should consult a screenshot to determine the coordinates of the element first; after the tab loads a different site, take a new screenshot before clicking by `coordinate`.

tabId.description: Tab to act on within the preview context. Omit for the fronted tab; get ids from tabs_context.

action.description:
The action to perform:
* `left_click`: Click the left mouse button at the specified coordinates.
* `right_click`: Click the right mouse button at the specified coordinates to open context menus.
* `double_click`: Double-click the left mouse button at the specified coordinates.
* `triple_click`: Triple-click the left mouse button at the specified coordinates.
* `type`: Type a string of text.
* `screenshot`: Take a screenshot of the screen.
* `wait`: Wait for a specified number of seconds.
* `scroll`: Scroll up, down, left, or right at the specified coordinates.
* `key`: Press a specific keyboard key.
* `left_click_drag`: Drag from start_coordinate to coordinate.
* `zoom`: Take a screenshot of a specific region for closer inspection.
* `scroll_to`: Scroll an element into view using its element reference ID from read_page or find tools.
* `hover`: Move the mouse cursor to the specified coordinates or element without clicking. Useful for revealing tooltips, dropdown menus, or triggering hover states.

coordinate.description: (x, y): The x (pixels from the left edge) and y (pixels from the top edge) coordinates. Required for `left_click`, `right_click`, `double_click`, `triple_click`, and `scroll`. For `left_click_drag`, this is the end position.

text.description: The text to type (for `type` action) or the key(s) to press (for `key` action). For `key` action: Provide space-separated keys (e.g., "Backspace Backspace Delete"). Supports keyboard shortcuts using the platform's modifier key (use "cmd" on Mac, "ctrl" on Windows/Linux, e.g., "cmd+a" or "ctrl+a" for select all). Page zoom shortcuts (e.g. "cmd+=", "ctrl+-", "cmd+0") are not supported - use the `zoom` action to magnify a region of the page instead.

duration.description: The number of seconds to wait. Required for `wait`. Maximum 10 seconds.

scroll_direction.description: The direction to scroll. Required for `scroll`.

scroll_amount.description: The number of scroll wheel ticks. Optional for `scroll`, defaults to 3.

region.description: (x0, y0, x1, y1): The rectangular region to capture for `zoom`. Coordinates define a rectangle from top-left (x0, y0) to bottom-right (x1, y1) in pixels from the viewport origin. Required for `zoom` action. Useful for inspecting small UI elements like icons, buttons, or text.

scale.description: For `screenshot` and `zoom` only. Scale factor in [0.1, 1] for the returned image; 1 (default) uses the full image token budget, 0.5 returns an image at half the width and height (~quarter of the tokens). Coordinates are ALWAYS in the full-resolution coordinate frame (reported with every scaled screenshot), never in the scaled image's own pixels.

repeat.description: Number of times to repeat the key sequence. Only applicable for `key` action. Must be a positive integer between 1 and 100. Default is 1. Useful for navigation tasks like pressing arrow keys multiple times.

ref.description: Element reference ID from read_page or find tools (e.g., "ref_1", "ref_2"). Required for `scroll_to` action. Can be used as alternative to `coordinate` for click actions.

modifiers.description: Modifier keys for click actions. Supports: "ctrl", "shift", "alt", "cmd" (or "meta"), "win" (or "windows"). Can be combined with "+" (e.g., "ctrl+shift", "cmd+alt"). Optional.

action_summary.description: A few words saying what this action does on the page and to what, for example 'Sends the drafted reply to pat@example.com' or 'Opens the Filters menu'. Set it on every left_click, right_click, double_click, triple_click, left_click_drag, key and type action. State the effect only, and accurately: no reasons, nothing about what you were asked or allowed to do, no passwords or other secrets.

An emulated size applies to that tab across reloads and navigation (scaled down to fit when it is larger than the pane): reset it with preset "desktop" as soon as you finish testing. The desktop app may also clear a size you set when your turn ends, so set it again in a later turn if you still need it. A size the user picked from the pane's own Viewport menu is theirs and stays until they or you change it; leave it unless they ask. colorScheme (light/dark) emulates prefers-color-scheme on that tab; it survives reloads and preset "desktop" does not touch it, but the pane re-syncs the tab to the app's light/dark theme when that theme changes or the pane reopens; local documents and static HTML previews always render light. The mobile preset (and any width < 768) also emulates a mobile device: Android Chrome user agent and 5 touch points, so pages detect a touch phone; your clicks still arrive as mouse clicks. Reload the page after switching so load-time device gates re-run.

tools.name: mcp__Claude_Code_iOS_Simulator__control
tools.description: Run, test, and visually verify iOS apps in the iOS Simulator on this Mac. Use this whenever the user wants to see or try their iOS app — "run my app", "test this on iPhone", "does this look right?", "try the new screen" — not only when they mention the simulator by name. Simulator only: this tool cannot drive or stream a physical iPhone or iPad. If the user wants the app on their real device ("on my iPhone", "on my device"), build and deploy for the device with your normal build tools instead, and say the live panel only shows simulators. 'attach' opens a live panel so the user can watch — when the user wants to see the app, call 'attach' FIRST, before building: it is cheap, opens instantly on a booted simulator, and errors harmlessly when nothing is booted (boot or build, then retry it). 'launch' installs and launches a built .app — build it first, with the user's own build tooling or this server's 'build' tool when this session has it; launch re-attaches on its own, but do not rely on that instead of the early attach. Screenshots and tap/swipe/text verification are headless and need no panel. Don't open the panel when the user only asked to build/compile or to run unit tests. Coordinates are in device points (origin top-left); the 'launch' result reports the device's point dimensions.

schema.name: mcp__Claude_Code_iOS_Simulator__control
schema.description: Run, test, and visually verify iOS apps in the iOS Simulator on this Mac. Use this whenever the user wants to see or try their iOS app — "run my app", "test this on iPhone", "does this look right?", "try the new screen" — not only when they mention the simulator by name. Simulator only: this tool cannot drive or stream a physical iPhone or iPad. If the user wants the app on their real device ("on my iPhone", "on my device"), build and deploy for the device with your normal build tools instead, and say the live panel only shows simulators. 'attach' opens a live panel so the user can watch — when the user wants to see the app, call 'attach' FIRST, before building: it is cheap, opens instantly on a booted simulator, and errors harmlessly when nothing is booted (boot or build, then retry it). 'launch' installs and launches a built .app — build it first, with the user's own build tooling or this server's 'build' tool when this session has it; launch re-attaches on its own, but do not rely on that instead of the early attach. Screenshots and tap/swipe/text verification are headless and need no panel. Don't open the panel when the user only asked to build/compile or to run unit tests. Coordinates are in device points (origin top-left); the 'launch' result reports the device's point dimensions.

action.description: What to do. 'attach' opens the live simulator panel for the user — call it BEFORE you build or launch, as soon as the user wants to see the app: on a booted simulator it opens immediately, and otherwise it returns a clear, harmless error (boot or build first, then retry it). Do not skip the early attach because 'launch' also attaches — the panel should be open before the build starts. The panel is the user's view, not a precondition — 'screenshot' and input actions work without it. Skip it only when the user has no interest in watching; 'launch' installs and launches an .app (it also re-attaches, but call 'attach' early rather than relying on that); 'screenshot' returns a PNG of the current screen; 'tap'/'swipe'/'text'/'button' inject input; 'press_key' presses a hardware key 'count' times: return, delete (backspace), an arrow, select_all, undo or redo (a key also hides the on-screen keyboard); 'set_appearance' switches the device to light or dark mode; 'appearance' says which it is in; 'set_keyboard' shows or hides the on-screen keyboard (it appears only while a text field has focus, and 'press_key' and 'text' hide it again); 'rotate' turns the device a quarter turn left or right ('direction'); take a 'screenshot' after it and tap in that screenshot's frame, however it comes back; 'touch_path' performs a single-finger drag along an arbitrary path (eased curves, long-press-then-drag); 'touch2_path' is the two-finger variant for pinch/rotate; 'open_url' opens a deep link; 'detach' closes the panel/stream. NOTE: a 'swipe' or 'touch_path' whose start point is on-screen and within 4pt of an edge performs the OS edge gesture instead of a plain drag — left=back, top=notification shade, bottom=home/app-switcher, right=Control Center (mapped to the current interface orientation). Start more than 4pt from the edge to drag or scroll content near the bezel.

app_path.description: For 'launch': absolute path (no ~) to the built .app bundle (e.g. /Users/me/Library/Developer/Xcode/DerivedData/MyApp-abc123/Build/Products/Debug-iphonesimulator/MyApp.app).

device.description: Simulator name (e.g. 'iPhone 17 Pro') or UDID. Defaults to the simulator already attached, else the first booted one. The first use of a device asks the user for permission.

udid.description: Alias for 'device' (identical semantics: simulator name or UDID). Pass at most one of 'device' / 'udid'.

bundle_id.description: For 'launch': bundle identifier. If omitted, extracted from the .app's Info.plist.

points.description: For 'touch_path': touch path samples in device points. First point is touch-down; last is touch-up. dt_ms is the delay before that sample (0-1000 ms; the first sample's is skipped, so send 0 or omit it; at most 30 seconds in all).

points2.description: For 'touch2_path': two-finger path samples in device points. Each sample carries both contacts (x1/y1, x2/y2); first is touch-down, last is touch-up. dt_ms is the delay before that sample (0-1000 ms; the first sample's is skipped, so send 0 or omit it; at most 30 seconds in all).

duration.description: Seconds. For 'tap', >0.5 is a long-press. For 'swipe', the gesture duration (default 0.3).

key.description: For 'press_key': the key or edit command to press.

count.description: For 'press_key': how many times to press it, 1 to 20 (default 1).

state.description: For 'set_keyboard': 'show' or 'hide' the on-screen keyboard. For 'set_appearance': 'light' or 'dark'.

url.description: For 'open_url': URL or scheme to open in the simulator.

The code is auto-detected: starts with <svg = SVG mode, otherwise HTML mode.
A global sendPrompt(text) function is available — it sends a message to chat as if the user typed it.
IMPORTANT: Call read_me before your first show_widget call. Do NOT narrate or mention the read_me call to the user — call it silently, then respond as if you went straight to building the visualization.

loading_messages.description: 1–4 loading messages shown to the user while the visual renders, each roughly 5 words long. Write them in the same language the user is using. Use 1 for simple visuals, more for complex ones. If the topic is serious — illness, disease, pandemics, death, grief, war, conflict, poverty, disaster, trauma, abuse, addiction, medical decisions, politically charged subjects, or anything where the reader might be personally affected — keep these BORING: describe what the code is doing in the dullest generic way, no jargon-as-drama, no evocative terms. Pandemic growth model — NOT ['Simulating patient zero', 'Modeling the curve'] (documentary-narrator voice), YES ['Setting up the model', 'Running the calculation']. Cancer timeline — NOT ['Charting the battle ahead'], YES ['Laying out the stages']. If you have to ask whether it's serious, it is. Otherwise, have fun — reach for alliteration, puns, personification, wordplay, whatever lands in that language. Playful examples — revenue chart: ['Bribing bars to stand taller', 'Asking Q4 where it went']; kanban: ['Herding cards into columns', 'Dragging, dropping, not stopping'].

title.description: Short snake_case identifier for this visual. Must be specific and disambiguating — if the conversation has multiple visuals, this title alone should tell you which one is being referenced (e.g. 'q4_revenue_by_product_line' not 'chart', 'oauth_login_flow' not 'diagram'). Also used as the download filename, so no spaces or special characters.

widget_code.description: SVG or HTML code to render. For SVG: raw SVG code starting with <svg> tag, must use CSS variables for colors. Example: <svg viewBox="0 0 700 400" xmlns="http://www.w3.org/2000/svg">...</svg>. For HTML: raw HTML content to render, do NOT include DOCTYPE, <html>, <head>, or <body> tags. Use CSS variables for theming. Keep background transparent and avoid top-level padding. Scripts are supported but execute after streaming completes.

# Access kernel: `alloc` (O14)

separately, its auxiliary `KAux`; it adds exactly one root place and exactly one authority, the root
`Modify` authority of that place, with no origin, held by `owner`, the new leaves `Uninit` (§71,
`ok`); `fail` happens only when the static preconditions hold and `K.Satisfiable` is false, and

namespace Alloc

/-! ## Shape of the new places (§71.1, §71 `ok`) -/

/-- Every element of a local shape is owned by the receiving holder (§71.1: the shape is
represented like the locals of `enterFrame`, which have no owning element). -/
theorem shapeOwner_toShape (ls : LocalShape) (hd : Holder) (i : Nat) :
    shapeOwner ls.toShape hd i = hd := by
  simp only [shapeOwner, LocalShape.toShape, List.getElem?_map]
  cases ls[i]? <;> rfl

/-- A local shape has one element per entry (§71.1). -/
theorem length_toShape (ls : LocalShape) : ls.toShape.length = ls.length := by
  simp [LocalShape.toShape]

/-- The places after `alloc` are the former places followed by the elements of the shape (§71,
`ok`: fresh identities). -/
theorem allocP_len (s : S3) (ow : Nat) (ls : LocalShape) :
    (allocP s ow ls).length = s.P.length + ls.length := by
  simp [allocP, shapeP, LocalShape.toShape]

theorem allocP_lt {s : S3} {ow : Nat} {ls : LocalShape} {q : Nat} (h : q < s.P.length) :
    (allocP s ow ls)[q]? = s.P[q]? := List.getElem?_append_left h

326	    · subst e; simp
327	    · have hgf : (g != f) = true := by simp [e]
328	      simp only [hgf, ↓reduceIte]
329	      exact ancestor_self (List.mem_cons.1 h |>.resolve_left (fun h' => e h'.symm))

334	/-- The anchor-order condition of an existing authority carries over `alloc` (§44, §71 `ok`):
335	effective anchors, their holders and the frames of the former places are unchanged. -/
336	theorem effAnchorOK_old (hst : AllocStatic k s pr ow ls) (hw : WF3 s) {x : Nat}
337	    {fd : Option Nat} (h : EffAnchorOK s x fd) : EffAnchorOK (allocEff s ow ls) x fd := by
338	  have he : (allocEff s ow ls).effAnchor x = s.effAnchor x := by
339	    simp only [S3.effAnchor, ancs_eq hst]
340	  unfold EffAnchorOK at h ⊢
341	  rw [he]
342	  cases hz : s.A[s.effAnchor x]? with
343	  | none => rw [hz] at h; exact h.elim
344	  | some z =>
345	    rw [hz] at h
346	    rw [A_lt (lt_of_getElem? hz), hz]
347	    have hh : (allocEff s ow ls).hframe z.holder = s.hframe z.holder := by
348	      cases hzh : z.holder with
349	      | frame f => rfl
350	      | place p =>
351	        show (allocEff s ow ls).pframe p = s.pframe p
352	        cases hg : s.pframe p with
353	        | none => simp only [OptP, hzh, S3.hframe, hg] at h
354	        | some g => rw [← hg]; exact pframe_old hw (pframe_iff.1 hg).lt
355	    simp only [OptP] at h ⊢
356	    rw [hh]
357	    exact h
358	
359	/-- The new root authority satisfies the anchor-order condition for its holder `owner` (§44,
360	§71 `ok`): it is its own effective anchor, held by `owner`, whose frame is on the stack. -/
361	theorem effAnchorOK_new (hst : AllocStatic k s pr ow ls) :
362	    EffAnchorOK (allocEff s ow ls) s.A.length ((allocEff s ow ls).pframe ow) := by
363	  have hA : (allocEff s ow ls).A[s.A.length]? =
364	      some ⟨.modify, none, footprint (allocP s ow ls) s.P.length, .place ow, true⟩ := by
365	    rw [allocEff_A hst]; simp
366	  have he : (allocEff s ow ls).effAnchor s.A.length = s.A.length := by
367	    simp only [S3.effAnchor, S3.ancs,
368	      chain_none (show (allocEff s ow ls).org s.A.length = none by simp [S3.org, hA]),
369	      List.getLastD_nil]
370	  obtain ⟨f, hf, hfF⟩ := (usable_old (ls := ls) hst.ownerUsable).frameOf
371	  have hpf := pframe_iff.2 hf
372	  unfold EffAnchorOK
373	  rw [he, hA, hpf]
374	  simp only [OptP, S3.hframe, hpf]
375	  exact ancestor_self hfF
376	
377	end Anchor

382	variable {k : K} {s : S3} {pr ow : Nat} {ls : LocalShape}

384	/-- `alloc` preserves `RootChain` (§49.6, §71 `ok`): former authorities keep their chains and the
385	footprints of former places are unchanged; the new root authority is the root authority of the
386	new root place. -/
387	theorem rootChain (hst : AllocStatic k s pr ow ls) (hw : WF3 s) :
388	    RootChain (allocEff s ow ls) := by
389	  intro a y l ha hl hleaf
390	  rcases allocA_get hst ha with ⟨ha', hy⟩ | ⟨rfl, rfl⟩
391	  · obtain ⟨hlt, -⟩ := hw.footprints a y hy l hl
392	    obtain ⟨x0, z, r, hx0, hz, hzo, ⟨hrl, hrp⟩, hlr, hfz⟩ :=
393	      hw.rootChain a y l hy hl ((isLeaf_old hst.shapeOK hlt).1 hleaf)
394	    have hx0lt : x0 < s.A.length := by
395	      rcases hx0 with rfl | hx0
396	      · exact ha'
397	      · exact Nat.lt_trans (chain_lt hx0) ha'
398	    refine ⟨x0, z, r, by rw [ancs_eq hst]; exact hx0, by rw [A_lt hx0lt]; exact hz, hzo,
399	      ⟨by show r < (allocP s ow ls).length; rw [allocP_len]; omega,
400	       by show parentOf (allocP s ow ls) r = none; rw [parentOf_lt hrl]; exact hrp⟩,
401	      (partOf_old hlt).2 hlr, fun l' => ?_⟩
402	    show _ ↔ l' ∈ footprint (allocP s ow ls) r
403	    rw [footprint_old hst.shapeOK hrl]; exact hfz l'
404	  · exact ⟨s.A.length, _, s.P.length, .inl rfl, ha, rfl, root_new hst, (mem_footprint.1 hl).2.2,
405	      fun _ => Iff.rfl⟩
406	
407	/-- `alloc` preserves `RootHeld` (§49.7, §71 `ok`): former usable root places keep their root
408	authority; the new root place has the new root authority, held by its owner `owner`. -/
409	theorem rootHeld (hst : AllocStatic k s pr ow ls) (hw : WF3 s) :
410	    RootHeld (allocEff s ow ls) := by
411	  intro r hr hu
412	  by_cases hrl : r < s.P.length
413	  · have hr0 : RootPlace s.P r :=
414	      ⟨hrl, by rw [← parentOf_lt (ow := ow) (ls := ls) hrl]; exact hr.2⟩
415	    obtain ⟨i, z, pr', hz, za, zo, zm, hpr, hh, hf⟩ := hw.rootHeld r hr0 (usable_back hw hu hrl)
416	    exact ⟨i, z, pr', by rw [A_lt (lt_of_getElem? hz)]; exact hz, za, zo, zm,
417	      by show (allocP s ow ls)[r]? = _; rw [allocP_lt hrl]; exact hpr, hh,
418	      fun l => by
419	        show _ ↔ l ∈ footprint (allocP s ow ls) r
420	        rw [footprint_old hst.shapeOK hrl]; exact hf l⟩
421	  · obtain rfl := root_unique_new hst (by omega) hr
422	    exact ⟨s.A.length, ⟨.modify, none, footprint (allocP s ow ls) s.P.length, .place ow, true⟩, _,
423	      by rw [allocEff_A hst]; simp, rfl, rfl, rfl, allocP_root hst, rfl, fun _ => Iff.rfl⟩
424	
425	/-- `alloc` preserves `WF3` (§49, §71.3 "new identities and ownership relations must respect
426	`WF3`, `RootHeld`"). -/
427	theorem wf3 (hst : AllocStatic k s pr ow ls) (hw : WF3 s) : WF3 (allocEff s ow ls) where
428	  frames := hw.frames
429	  places q pl r hq hp := by
430	    rcases allocP_get hq with ⟨hql, hq'⟩ | ⟨hqn, -, -, how⟩
431	    · obtain ⟨pr', hpr, hlt, ho, hd⟩ := hw.places q pl r hq' hp
432	      refine ⟨pr', by show (allocP s ow ls)[r]? = _; rw [allocP_lt (by omega)]; exact hpr, hlt,
433	        ho, ?_⟩
434	      simp [allocEff, show ¬ s.P.length ≤ r by omega, show ¬ s.P.length ≤ q by omega, hd]
435	    · have hpo : parentOf (allocP s ow ls) q = some r := by
436	        simp only [parentOf]; rw [show (allocP s ow ls)[q]? = some pl from hq]; exact hp
437	      obtain ⟨hr, hrq⟩ := parentOf_ge hst.shapeOK hqn hpo
438	      have hrl : q < s.P.length + ls.length := by
439	        have := lt_of_getElem? hq; rwa [show (allocEff s ow ls).P = allocP s ow ls from rfl,
440	          allocP_len] at this
441	      obtain ⟨i, rfl⟩ : ∃ i, r = s.P.length + i := ⟨r - s.P.length, by omega⟩
442	      exact ⟨_, allocP_new (by omega), hrq, by rw [how],
443	        by simp [allocEff, hqn]⟩
444	  owners := ⟨fun q pl f hq ho => (by
445	      rcases allocP_get hq with ⟨-, hq'⟩ | ⟨-, -, -, how⟩
446	      · exact hw.owners.1 q pl f hq' ho
447	      · rw [how] at ho; cases ho),
448	    fun q pl o hq ho => (by
449	      show o < (allocP s ow ls).length
450	      rw [allocP_len]
451	      rcases allocP_get hq with ⟨-, hq'⟩ | ⟨-, -, -, how⟩
452	      · have := hw.owners.2.1 q pl o hq' ho; omega
453	      · rw [how] at ho; cases ho; have := hst.ownerUsable.lt; omega),
454	    fun _ hq => S3.Usable.frameOf hq⟩
455	  footprints a x hx l hl := by
456	    rcases allocA_get hst hx with ⟨-, hx'⟩ | ⟨-, rfl⟩
457	    · obtain ⟨hlt, hleaf⟩ := hw.footprints a x hx' l hl
458	      exact ⟨by show l < (allocP s ow ls).length; rw [allocP_len]; omega,
459	        (isLeaf_old hst.shapeOK hlt).2 hleaf⟩
460	    · obtain ⟨h1, h2, -⟩ := mem_footprint.1 hl
461	      exact ⟨h1, h2⟩
462	  origins b y a hb ho := by
463	    rcases allocA_get hst hb with ⟨-, hb'⟩ | ⟨-, rfl⟩
464	    · exact hw.origins b y a hb' ho
465	    · cases ho
466	  rootChain := rootChain hst hw
467	  rootHeld := rootHeld hst hw
468	  holders a y hy ya := by
469	    rcases allocA_get hst hy with ⟨-, hy'⟩ | ⟨-, rfl⟩
470	    · have := hw.holders a y hy' ya
471	      cases hh : y.holder with
472	      | frame f => rw [hh] at this; exact this
473	      | place p => rw [hh] at this; exact usable_old this
474	    · exact usable_old hst.ownerUsable
475	
476	/-- `alloc` preserves `I1` (§50, §71 `ok`): the new root authority covers only new leaves. -/
477	theorem i1 (hst : AllocStatic k s pr ow ls) (hw : WF3 s) (h1 : I1 s) :
478	    I1 (allocEff s ow ls) := by
479	  intro a b x y p hab ha hb xa ya xp yp hnab hnba
480	  rcases allocA_get hst ha with ⟨-, hx⟩ | ⟨rfl, rfl⟩ <;>
481	    rcases allocA_get hst hb with ⟨-, hy⟩ | ⟨rfl, rfl⟩
482	  · rw [ancs_eq hst] at hnab hnba
483	    exact h1 a b x y p hab hx hy xa ya xp yp hnab hnba
484	  · have := (hw.footprints a x hx p xp).1
485	    have := fp_new_ge (s := s) (ow := ow) (ls := ls) yp; omega
486	  · have := (hw.footprints b y hy p yp).1
487	    have := fp_new_ge (s := s) (ow := ow) (ls := ls) xp; omega
488	  · exact absurd rfl hab

490	/-- `alloc` preserves `I2` (§51, §71 `ok`): the new authority has no origin. -/
491	theorem i2 (hst : AllocStatic k s pr ow ls) (h2 : I2 s) : I2 (allocEff s ow ls) := by
492	  intro b y a hb ho
493	  rcases allocA_get hst hb with ⟨-, hb'⟩ | ⟨-, rfl⟩
494	  · obtain ⟨x₁, hx₁, hh⟩ := h2 b y a hb' ho
495	    exact ⟨x₁, by rw [A_lt (lt_of_getElem? hx₁)]; exact hx₁, hh⟩
496	  · cases ho

498	/-- `alloc` preserves `I3` (§52, §71 `ok`): the new places have no anchor. -/
499	theorem i3 (hw : WF3 s) (h3 : I3 s) : I3 (allocEff s ow ls) := by
500	  intro q hq x hx
501	  by_cases hql : q < s.P.length
502	  · have hx' : x ∈ s.D q := by simpa [allocEff, show ¬ s.P.length ≤ q by omega] using hx
503	    obtain ⟨y, hy, ya⟩ := h3 q (usable_back hw hq hql) x hx'
504	    exact ⟨y, by rw [A_lt (lt_of_getElem? hy)]; exact hy, ya⟩
505	  · simp [allocEff, show s.P.length ≤ q by omega] at hx

507	/-- `alloc` preserves `AnchorOrder` (§44, §54, §71 `ok`): the new places have no anchor and the
508	frames of the former places do not change. -/
509	theorem anchorOrder (hst : AllocStatic k s pr ow ls) (hw : WF3 s) (hao : AnchorOrder s) :
510	    AnchorOrder (allocEff s ow ls) := by
511	  intro q hq x hx
512	  by_cases hql : q < s.P.length
513	  · have hx' : x ∈ s.D q := by simpa [allocEff, show ¬ s.P.length ≤ q by omega] using hx
514	    rw [pframe_old hw hql]
515	    exact effAnchorOK_old hst hw (hao q (usable_back hw hq hql) x hx')
516	  · simp [allocEff, show s.P.length ≤ q by omega] at hx

518	/-- `alloc` preserves `NoDangling` (§54, §71 `ok`): former places keep their footprints and
519	usability; the new root authority covers only new places, which are usable. -/
520	theorem noDangling (hst : AllocStatic k s pr ow ls) (hw : WF3 s) (hnd : NoDangling s) :
521	    NoDangling (allocEff s ow ls) := by
522	  intro j z hz za q hq l hl hlz
523	  obtain ⟨hlP, -, hlq⟩ := mem_footprint.1 hl
524	  have hql : q ≤ l := by
525	    rcases hlq.2 with rfl | hc
526	    · exact Nat.le_refl _
527	    · exact Nat.le_of_lt (chain_lt hc)
528	  rcases allocA_get hst hz with ⟨-, hy⟩ | ⟨-, rfl⟩
529	  · have hlo := (hw.footprints j z hy l hlz).1
530	    have hqo : q < s.P.length := by omega
531	    exact hnd j z hy za q (fun hu => hq (usable_old hu)) l
532	      ((footprint_old hst.shapeOK hqo l).1 hl) hlz
533	  · have hge := fp_new_ge (s := s) (ow := ow) (ls := ls) hlz
534	    by_cases hqo : q < s.P.length
535	    · have := (mem_footprint.1 ((footprint_old hst.shapeOK hqo l).1 hl)).1; omega
536	    · have hlP' : l < (allocP s ow ls).length := hlP
537	      rw [allocP_len] at hlP'
538	      exact hq (usable_new hst.ownerUsable (by omega) (by omega))
539	
540	/-- `alloc` preserves `AnchorOrderHeld` (§44, §54, §71 `ok`): former held authorities keep their
541	condition; the new root authority is its own effective anchor, held by `owner`. -/
542	theorem anchorOrderHeld (hst : AllocStatic k s pr ow ls) (hw : WF3 s) (h : AnchorOrderHeld s) :
543	    AnchorOrderHeld (allocEff s ow ls) := by
544	  intro q hq x y hx ya hh
545	  rcases allocA_get hst hx with ⟨-, hx'⟩ | ⟨rfl, rfl⟩
546	  · have hq0 : s.Usable q := by have := hw.holders x y hx' ya; rw [hh] at this; exact this
547	    rw [pframe_old hw hq0.lt]
548	    exact effAnchorOK_old hst hw (h q hq0 x y hx' ya hh)
549	  · cases hh
550	    exact effAnchorOK_new hst

553	covers only leaves of the new root place, whose owner `owner` holds it. -/
554	theorem rootHeldConv (hst : AllocStatic k s pr ow ls) (hw : WF3 s) (hc : RootHeldConv s) :
555	    RootHeldConv (allocEff s ow ls) := by
556	  intro x z l r hx ho hl hr hlr
557	  rcases allocA_get hst hx with ⟨-, hx'⟩ | ⟨rfl, rfl⟩
558	  · have hlt := (hw.footprints x z hx' l hl).1
559	    have hlr' := (partOf_old hlt).1 hlr
560	    have hrl : r < s.P.length := by
561	      rcases hlr'.2 with rfl | hc'
562	      · exact hlt
563	      · exact Nat.lt_trans (chain_lt hc') hlt
564	    have hr' : RootPlace s.P r :=
565	      ⟨hrl, by rw [← parentOf_lt (ow := ow) (ls := ls) hrl]; exact hr.2⟩
566	    obtain ⟨pr', hpr, hh⟩ := hc x z l r hx' ho hl hr' hlr'
567	    exact ⟨pr', by show (allocP s ow ls)[r]? = _; rw [allocP_lt hrl]; exact hpr, hh⟩
568	  · obtain rfl := rootOf_unique hr (root_new hst) hlr (mem_footprint.1 hl).2.2
569	    exact ⟨_, allocP_root hst, rfl⟩

579	/-! ## Main results (§57, §58, §71) -/
580	
581	/-- `alloc` preserves the main invariant (§57, §58: an `ok` transition preserves the invariants;
582	§71.3: the new identities and ownership relations respect `WF3` and `RootHeld`): from a state
583	satisfying `KInv`, the `ok` outcome of `alloc` satisfies `KInv`. -/
584	theorem alloc_preserves {k : K} {pr ow : Nat} {ls : LocalShape} {s s' : S3}
585	    (hk : KInv s) (h : AllocStep k pr ow ls s (.ok s')) : KInv s' := by
586	  cases h with
587	  | ok hst _ =>
588	    obtain ⟨hw, ⟨⟨h1, h2, h3, -⟩, hao, hnd⟩, haoh, -⟩ := hk
589	    exact kInv_of (Alloc.wf3 hst hw)
590	        ⟨⟨Alloc.i1 hst hw h1, Alloc.i2 hst h2, Alloc.i3 hw h3, i4_always _⟩,
591	          Alloc.anchorOrder hst hw hao, Alloc.noDangling hst hw hnd⟩
592	        (Alloc.anchorOrderHeld hst hw haoh)
593	
594	/-- `alloc` preserves the auxiliary `KAux` (`RootHeldConv`, §40, §49.7; §71 `ok`) from a `KInv`
595	state. -/
596	theorem alloc_preserves_kAux {k : K} {pr ow : Nat} {ls : LocalShape} {s s' : S3}
597	    (hk : KInv s) (ha : KAux s) (h : AllocStep k pr ow ls s (.ok s')) : KAux s' := by
598	  cases h with
599	  | ok hst _ => exact Alloc.rootHeldConv hst hk.1 ha
600	
601	/-- The `ok` effect of `alloc` (§71, `ok`): the former places are kept and the nonempty shape is
602	appended with fresh identities, every new place owned by `owner`; among the new places exactly
603	one, `|P|`, is a root place (a new storage root); exactly one authority is added, at the fresh
604	identity `|A|`: the root `Modify` authority of `|P|`, with no origin, held by `owner`, covering
605	the footprint of `|P|`; the leaves of `|P|` are `Uninit`. -/
606	theorem alloc_one_root {k : K} {pr ow : Nat} {ls : LocalShape} {s s' : S3}
607	    (h : AllocStep k pr ow ls s (.ok s')) :
608	    s'.P.length = s.P.length + ls.length ∧ 0 < ls.length ∧
609	    (∀ q < s.P.length, s'.P[q]? = s.P[q]?) ∧
610	    (∀ (q : Nat) (pl : Place), s.P.length ≤ q → s'.P[q]? = some pl → pl.owner = .place ow) ∧
611	    RootPlace s'.P s.P.length ∧
612	    (∀ r, s.P.length ≤ r → RootPlace s'.P r → r = s.P.length) ∧
613	    s'.A = s.A ++ [⟨.modify, none, footprint s'.P s.P.length, .place ow, true⟩] ∧
614	    ∀ l ∈ footprint s'.P s.P.length, s'.I l = .uninit := by
615	  cases h with
616	  | ok hst _ =>
617	    refine ⟨Alloc.allocP_len s ow ls, Alloc.len_pos hst, fun q hq => Alloc.allocP_lt hq,
618	      fun q pl hq hpl => ?_, Alloc.root_new hst,
619	      fun r hr hrp => Alloc.root_unique_new hst hr hrp, Alloc.allocEff_A hst, fun l hl => ?_⟩
620	    · rcases Alloc.allocP_get hpl with ⟨hq', -⟩ | ⟨-, -, -, how⟩
621	      · omega
622	      · exact how
623	    · have := Alloc.fp_new_ge (s := s) (ow := ow) (ls := ls) hl
624	      simp [allocEff, this]
625	
626	/-- `alloc` is deterministic (§58, §71): its outcome is a function of the state and the
627	arguments. -/
628	theorem alloc_det {k : K} {pr ow : Nat} {ls : LocalShape} {s : S3} {o₁ o₂ : Outcome3 S3}
629	    (h₁ : AllocStep k pr ow ls s o₁) (h₂ : AllocStep k pr ow ls s o₂) : o₁ = o₂ := by
630	  cases h₁ <;> cases h₂ <;> first | rfl | contradiction
631	
632	/-- A failed `alloc` leaves the state unchanged (§58: `fail` is a defined failure leaving the
633	state unchanged; §71: `fail` when the static preconditions hold but `K.Satisfiable` is false, no
634	state change). The `fail` outcome carries no state, so the state stays `s`; moreover the failure
635	happens only when the static preconditions hold and `K.Satisfiable(provider, shape, s)` is false,
636	and then no `ok` successor state exists. -/
637	theorem alloc_fail_unchanged {k : K} {pr ow : Nat} {ls : LocalShape} {s : S3}
638	    (h : AllocStep k pr ow ls s .fail) :
639	    AllocStatic k s pr ow ls ∧ ¬ k.Satisfiable pr ls s ∧
640	      ∀ s', ¬ AllocStep k pr ow ls s (.ok s') := by
641	  cases h with
642	  | fail h1 h2 => exact ⟨h1, h2, fun _ h' => by cases alloc_det (.fail h1 h2) h'⟩
643	
644	/-- Only `alloc` may produce `fail` in the O1–O16 kernel (§58: "Other kernel operations produce
645	`ok` or `reject`"): none of the other fifteen operation relations of `KStep` yields `fail`. -/
646	theorem fail_only_alloc (k : K) (s : S3) :
647	    (∀ src region m, ¬ DeriveStep src region m s .fail) ∧
648	    (∀ src rs, ¬ SplitStep k src rs s .fail) ∧
649	    (∀ a, ¬ ReleaseStep a s .fail) ∧
650	    (∀ src dst, ¬ TransferStep k src dst s .fail) ∧
651	    (∀ q x, ¬ DependStep q x s .fail) ∧
652	    (∀ ps ls, ¬ EnterStep ps ls s .fail) ∧
653	    ¬ ExitStep k s .fail ∧
654	    (∀ a ls, ¬ Read3Step a ls s .fail) ∧
655	    (∀ a ls, ¬ Write3Step a ls s .fail) ∧
656	    (∀ a ls, ¬ WriteSharedStep k a ls s .fail) ∧
657	    (∀ p, ¬ PinStep p s .fail) ∧
658	    (∀ p, ¬ UnpinStep k p s .fail) ∧
659	    (∀ p, ¬ EndUseStep k p s .fail) ∧
660	    (∀ p auth, ¬ FreeStep k p auth s .fail) ∧
661	    (∀ a p, ¬ StoreStep a p s .fail) :=
662	  ⟨fun _ _ _ => Alloc.guarded_ne_fail, fun _ _ => Alloc.guarded_ne_fail,
663	    fun _ => Alloc.guarded_ne_fail, fun _ _ => Alloc.guarded_ne_fail,

1	import Ern.MemoryModel.Access.Preserve.Common
2	
3	/-!
4	# Access kernel: `alloc` (O14)
5	
6	Results on `alloc provider owner shape` of `specs/ERN_Memory_Model_Specification_v0.md` §71 and
7	on the outcomes of §58: the `ok` outcome preserves the main invariant of §57 (`KInv`) and,
8	separately, its auxiliary `KAux`; it adds exactly one root place and exactly one authority, the root
9	`Modify` authority of that place, with no origin, held by `owner`, the new leaves `Uninit` (§71,
10	`ok`); `fail` happens only when the static preconditions hold and `K.Satisfiable` is false, and
11	produces no new state (§58, §71); `alloc` is deterministic; no other kernel operation O1–O16
12	yields `fail` (§58). Helper lemmas live in the namespace `Alloc`.
13	-/
14	
15	namespace Ern.MemoryModel.Access
16	
17	namespace Alloc
18	
19	/-! ## Shape of the new places (§71.1, §71 `ok`) -/
20	
21	/-- Every element of a local shape is owned by the receiving holder (§71.1: the shape is
22	represented like the locals of `enterFrame`, which have no owning element). -/
23	theorem shapeOwner_toShape (ls : LocalShape) (hd : Holder) (i : Nat) :
24	    shapeOwner ls.toShape hd i = hd := by
25	  simp only [shapeOwner, LocalShape.toShape, List.getElem?_map]
26	  cases ls[i]? <;> rfl
27	
28	/-- A local shape has one element per entry (§71.1). -/
29	theorem length_toShape (ls : LocalShape) : ls.toShape.length = ls.length := by
30	  simp [LocalShape.toShape]
31	
32	/-- The places after `alloc` are the former places followed by the elements of the shape (§71,
33	`ok`: fresh identities). -/
34	theorem allocP_len (s : S3) (ow : Nat) (ls : LocalShape) :
35	    (allocP s ow ls).length = s.P.length + ls.length := by
36	  simp [allocP, shapeP, LocalShape.toShape]
37	
38	/-- `alloc` keeps the former places (§71, `ok`). -/
39	theorem allocP_lt {s : S3} {ow : Nat} {ls : LocalShape} {q : Nat} (h : q < s.P.length) :
40	    (allocP s ow ls)[q]? = s.P[q]? := List.getElem?_append_left h
41	
42	/-- The new place of index `|P| + i` has the parent given by the shape and is owned by `owner`
43	(§71, `ok`: owned by `owner`). -/
44	theorem allocP_new {s : S3} {ow : Nat} {ls : LocalShape} {i : Nat} (h : i < ls.length) :
45	    (allocP s ow ls)[s.P.length + i]? =
46	      some ⟨(ls.toShape[i]?).bind (·.1), .place ow, ((ls.toShape[i]?).map (·.2.2)).getD 0⟩ := by
47	  have h' : i < ls.toShape.length := by rw [length_toShape]; exact h
48	  simp only [allocP, shapeP, List.getElem?_append_right (Nat.le_add_right _ _),
49	    Nat.add_sub_cancel_left, List.getElem?_map, List.getElem?_range h', Option.map_some,
50	    shapeOwner_toShape]
51	
52	/-- A place after `alloc` is a former place, or a new element of the shape owned by `owner`
53	(§71, `ok`). -/
54	theorem allocP_get {s : S3} {ow : Nat} {ls : LocalShape} {q : Nat} {pl : Place}
55	    (h : (allocP s ow ls)[q]? = some pl) :
56	    (q < s.P.length ∧ s.P[q]? = some pl) ∨
57	    (s.P.length ≤ q ∧ q < s.P.length + ls.length ∧
58	      pl.parent = (ls.toShape[q - s.P.length]?).bind (·.1) ∧ pl.owner = .place ow) := by
59	  by_cases hq : q < s.P.length
60	  · exact .inl ⟨hq, by rwa [allocP_lt hq] at h⟩
61	  · have hlt := lt_of_getElem? h
62	    rw [allocP_len] at hlt
63	    obtain ⟨i, rfl⟩ : ∃ i, q = s.P.length + i := ⟨q - s.P.length, by omega⟩
64	    rw [allocP_new (by omega)] at h
65	    cases h
66	    exact .inr ⟨by omega, hlt, by simp, rfl⟩
67	
68	/-- `alloc` keeps the parents of the former places (§71, `ok`). -/
69	theorem parentOf_lt {s : S3} {ow : Nat} {ls : LocalShape} {q : Nat} (h : q < s.P.length) :
70	    parentOf (allocP s ow ls) q = parentOf s.P q := by
71	  simp only [parentOf, allocP_lt h]
72	
73	/-- The parent of a new place is the one given by the shape (§71.1). -/
74	theorem parentOf_new {s : S3} {ow : Nat} {ls : LocalShape} {i : Nat} (h : i < ls.length) :
75	    parentOf (allocP s ow ls) (s.P.length + i) = (ls.toShape[i]?).bind (·.1) := by
76	  simp only [parentOf, allocP_new h, Option.bind_some]
77	
78	/-- The parent of a new place is an earlier new place (§71.1: well-formed shape). -/
79	theorem parentOf_ge {s : S3} {ow : Nat} {ls : LocalShape}
80	    (hsh : ShapeOK s.P.length ls.toShape) {q r : Nat} (hq : s.P.length ≤ q)
81	    (h : parentOf (allocP s ow ls) q = some r) : s.P.length ≤ r ∧ r < q := by
82	  have hlt : q < s.P.length + ls.length := by
83	    simp only [parentOf] at h
84	    cases h' : (allocP s ow ls)[q]? with
85	    | none => rw [h'] at h; cases h
86	    | some _ => have := lt_of_getElem? h'; rwa [allocP_len] at this
87	  obtain ⟨i, rfl⟩ : ∃ i, q = s.P.length + i := ⟨q - s.P.length, by omega⟩
88	  rw [parentOf_new (by omega)] at h
89	  have h1 := (hsh i (List.mem_range.2 (by rw [length_toShape]; omega))).1
90	  rw [h] at h1
91	  simp only [OptP] at h1
92	  obtain ⟨h₁, h₂, -⟩ := h1
93	  exact ⟨h₁, h₂⟩
94	
95	/-- The structural ancestors of a new place are new places (§71.1). -/
96	theorem chain_ge {s : S3} {ow : Nat} {ls : LocalShape} (hsh : ShapeOK s.P.length ls.toShape) :
97	    ∀ n q, q < n → s.P.length ≤ q → ∀ x ∈ chain (parentOf (allocP s ow ls)) q, s.P.length ≤ x
98	  | 0, _, h, _, _, _ => absurd h (Nat.not_lt_zero _)
99	  | n + 1, q, hq, hge, x, hx => by
100	    cases hpo : parentOf (allocP s ow ls) q with
101	    | none => rw [chain_none hpo] at hx; simp at hx
102	    | some r =>
103	      obtain ⟨hr, hrq⟩ := parentOf_ge hsh hge hpo
104	      rw [chain_cons hpo hrq] at hx
105	      rcases List.mem_cons.1 hx with rfl | hx
106	      · exact hr
107	      · exact chain_ge hsh n r (by omega) hr x hx
108	
109	/-- `alloc` keeps the structural ancestors of the former places (§71, `ok`). -/
110	theorem chain_old {s : S3} {ow : Nat} {ls : LocalShape} {l : Nat} (h : l < s.P.length) :
111	    chain (parentOf (allocP s ow ls)) l = chain (parentOf s.P) l :=
112	  chain_congr fun _ hj => parentOf_lt (Nat.lt_of_le_of_lt hj h)
113	
114	/-- `alloc` keeps the structural parts of the former places (§40, §71 `ok`). -/
115	theorem partOf_old {s : S3} {ow : Nat} {ls : LocalShape} {l r : Nat} (h : l < s.P.length) :
116	    partOf (allocP s ow ls) l r ↔ partOf s.P l r := by
117	  simp only [partOf, chain_old h, allocP_len]
118	  constructor
119	  · rintro ⟨-, hc⟩; exact ⟨h, hc⟩
120	  · rintro ⟨-, hc⟩; exact ⟨by omega, hc⟩
121	
122	/-- A former place is a leaf after `alloc` exactly when it was one before: new places have new
123	parents (§40, §71.1). -/
124	theorem isLeaf_old {s : S3} {ow : Nat} {ls : LocalShape} (hsh : ShapeOK s.P.length ls.toShape)
125	    {l : Nat} (h : l < s.P.length) : isLeaf (allocP s ow ls) l ↔ isLeaf s.P l := by
126	  constructor
127	  · intro hl r hr
128	    rw [← parentOf_lt (ow := ow) (ls := ls) hr]
129	    exact hl r (by rw [allocP_len]; omega)
130	  · intro hl r _ hp
131	    by_cases hrn : r < s.P.length
132	    · rw [parentOf_lt hrn] at hp; exact hl r hrn hp
133	    · have := (parentOf_ge hsh (by omega) hp).1; omega
134	
135	/-- `alloc` keeps the footprints of the former places (§40, §71 `ok`). -/
136	theorem footprint_old {s : S3} {ow : Nat} {ls : LocalShape} (hsh : ShapeOK s.P.length ls.toShape)
137	    {q : Nat} (hq : q < s.P.length) (l : Nat) :
138	    l ∈ footprint (allocP s ow ls) q ↔ l ∈ footprint s.P q := by
139	  rw [mem_footprint, mem_footprint]
140	  by_cases hl : l < s.P.length
141	  · rw [isLeaf_old hsh hl, partOf_old hl]
142	    exact ⟨fun h => ⟨hl, h.2⟩, fun h => ⟨by rw [allocP_len]; omega, h.2⟩⟩
143	  · constructor
144	    · rintro ⟨-, -, -, hc | hc⟩
145	      · omega
146	      · have := chain_ge hsh (l + 1) l (Nat.lt_succ_self l) (by omega) q hc; omega
147	    · rintro ⟨h, -⟩; exact absurd h hl
148	
149	/-- The leaves of the new place `|P|` are new places (§71, `ok`). -/
150	theorem fp_new_ge {s : S3} {ow : Nat} {ls : LocalShape} {l : Nat}
151	    (h : l ∈ footprint (allocP s ow ls) s.P.length) : s.P.length ≤ l := by
152	  obtain ⟨-, -, -, h | h⟩ := mem_footprint.1 h
153	  · omega
154	  · have := chain_lt h; omega
155	
156	/-! ## The single new root (§71.1, §71 `ok`) -/
157	
158	section Root
159	variable {k : K} {s : S3} {pr ow : Nat} {ls : LocalShape}
160	
161	/-- An accepted shape is nonempty (§71.1). -/
162	theorem len_pos (hst : AllocStatic k s pr ow ls) : 0 < ls.length := by
163	  cases ls with
164	  | nil => exact absurd rfl hst.nonempty
165	  | cons _ _ => exact Nat.succ_pos _
166	
167	/-- The first element of an accepted shape has no parent: a parent would be an earlier element
168	(§71.1). -/
169	theorem parent0 (hst : AllocStatic k s pr ow ls) : (ls.toShape[0]?).bind (·.1) = none := by
170	  have h1 := (hst.shapeOK 0 (List.mem_range.2 (by rw [length_toShape]; exact len_pos hst))).1
171	  cases hp : (ls.toShape[0]?).bind (·.1) with
172	  | none => rfl
173	  | some r =>
174	    rw [hp] at h1
175	    simp only [OptP] at h1
176	    obtain ⟨h₁, h₂, -⟩ := h1
177	    omega
178	
179	/-- The only root element of an accepted shape is its first element (§71.1, §71 `ok`: a new
180	storage root). -/
181	theorem rootIdx_eq (hst : AllocStatic k s pr ow ls) : rootIdx ls.toShape = [0] := by
182	  have h0 : 0 ∈ rootIdx ls.toShape := by
183	    simp only [rootIdx, List.mem_filter, List.mem_range, length_toShape]
184	    exact ⟨len_pos hst, by rw [parent0 hst]; rfl⟩
185	  have hl := hst.oneRoot
186	  generalize rootIdx ls.toShape = L at h0 hl ⊢
187	  match L, h0, hl with
188	  | [x], h0, _ => rw [List.mem_singleton] at h0; rw [h0]
189	  | [], h0, _ => exact absurd h0 (List.not_mem_nil)
190	  | _ :: _ :: _, _, hl => exact absurd hl (by simp only [List.length_cons]; omega)
191	
192	/-- The new place `|P|`: no parent, owned by `owner` (§71, `ok`). -/
193	theorem allocP_root (hst : AllocStatic k s pr ow ls) :
194	    (allocP s ow ls)[s.P.length]? =
195	      some ⟨none, .place ow, ((ls.toShape[0]?).map (·.2.2)).getD 0⟩ := by
196	  have := allocP_new (s := s) (ow := ow) (len_pos hst)
197	  rw [Nat.add_zero, parent0 hst] at this
198	  exact this
199	
200	/-- The new place `|P|` is a root place (§40, §71 `ok`). -/
201	theorem root_new (hst : AllocStatic k s pr ow ls) : RootPlace (allocP s ow ls) s.P.length :=
202	  ⟨by rw [allocP_len]; have := len_pos hst; omega,
203	    by simp only [parentOf, allocP_root hst, Option.bind_some]⟩
204	
205	/-- `|P|` is the only new root place (§71 `ok`: a new storage root). -/
206	theorem root_unique_new (hst : AllocStatic k s pr ow ls) {r : Nat} (hr : s.P.length ≤ r)
207	    (h : RootPlace (allocP s ow ls) r) : r = s.P.length := by
208	  obtain ⟨hlt, hp⟩ := h
209	  rw [allocP_len] at hlt
210	  obtain ⟨i, rfl⟩ : ∃ i, r = s.P.length + i := ⟨r - s.P.length, by omega⟩
211	  rw [parentOf_new (by omega)] at hp
212	  have : i ∈ rootIdx ls.toShape := by
213	    simp only [rootIdx, List.mem_filter, List.mem_range, length_toShape]
214	    exact ⟨by omega, by rw [hp]; rfl⟩
215	  rw [rootIdx_eq hst, List.mem_singleton] at this
216	  omega
217	
218	/-- The authorities after `alloc`: the former ones and one root `Modify` authority with no
219	origin, on the footprint of the new root, held by `owner` (§71, `ok`). -/
220	theorem allocEff_A (hst : AllocStatic k s pr ow ls) : (allocEff s ow ls).A =
221	    s.A ++ [⟨.modify, none, footprint (allocP s ow ls) s.P.length, .place ow, true⟩] := by
222	  simp only [allocEff, rootIdx_eq hst, List.map_cons, List.map_nil, Nat.add_zero,
223	    shapeOwner_toShape]
224	
225	/-- An authority after `alloc` is a former one, or the new root authority at the fresh identity
226	`|A|` (§42 fresh identities, §71 `ok`). -/
227	theorem allocA_get (hst : AllocStatic k s pr ow ls) {j : Nat} {z : Authority}
228	    (h : (allocEff s ow ls).A[j]? = some z) :
229	    (j < s.A.length ∧ s.A[j]? = some z) ∨
230	    (j = s.A.length ∧
231	      z = ⟨.modify, none, footprint (allocP s ow ls) s.P.length, .place ow, true⟩) :=
232	  addAuth_get (s := s) (by show (s.A ++ [_])[j]? = some z; rw [← allocEff_A hst]; exact h)
233	
234	/-- The new root authority has no origin, so `alloc` keeps every origin link (§42, §71 `ok`). -/
235	theorem org_eq (hst : AllocStatic k s pr ow ls) : (allocEff s ow ls).org = s.org := by
236	  funext i
237	  simp only [S3.org, allocEff_A hst]
238	  by_cases hi : i < s.A.length
239	  · rw [List.getElem?_append_left hi]
240	  · rw [List.getElem?_append_right (by omega), List.getElem?_eq_none (by omega : s.A.length ≤ i)]
241	    cases i - s.A.length <;> simp
242	
243	/-- `alloc` keeps every origin chain (§42, §71 `ok`). -/
244	theorem ancs_eq (hst : AllocStatic k s pr ow ls) : (allocEff s ow ls).ancs = s.ancs := by
245	  funext x; simp only [S3.ancs, org_eq hst]
246	
247	end Root
248	
249	/-- `alloc` keeps the former authorities (§71, `ok`). -/
250	theorem A_lt {s : S3} {ow : Nat} {ls : LocalShape} {j : Nat} (h : j < s.A.length) :
251	    (allocEff s ow ls).A[j]? = s.A[j]? := List.getElem?_append_left h
252	
253	/-! ## Usability and frames (§40, §44) -/
254	
255	section Usable
256	variable {s : S3} {ow : Nat} {ls : LocalShape}
257	
258	/-- A place usable before `alloc` stays usable (§40, §71 `ok`). -/
259	theorem usable_old {q : Nat} (h : s.Usable q) : (allocEff s ow ls).Usable q := by
260	  induction h with
261	  | @frame q f pl hpl hd ho hf =>
262	    exact .frame (show (allocP s ow ls)[q]? = _ by rw [allocP_lt (lt_of_getElem? hpl)]; exact hpl)
263	      (by simp [allocEff, hd, show ¬ s.P.length ≤ q from Nat.not_le.2 (lt_of_getElem? hpl)]) ho hf
264	  | @place q o pl hpl hd ho _ ih =>
265	    exact .place (show (allocP s ow ls)[q]? = _ by rw [allocP_lt (lt_of_getElem? hpl)]; exact hpl)
266	      (by simp [allocEff, hd, show ¬ s.P.length ≤ q from Nat.not_le.2 (lt_of_getElem? hpl)]) ho ih
267	
268	/-- A former place usable after `alloc` was usable before (§40, §49.3, §71 `ok`). -/
269	theorem usable_back (hw : WF3 s) {q : Nat} (h : (allocEff s ow ls).Usable q)
270	    (hq : q < s.P.length) : s.Usable q := by
271	  induction h with
272	  | @frame q f pl hpl hd ho hf =>
273	    have hpl' : s.P[q]? = some pl := by
274	      have : (allocP s ow ls)[q]? = some pl := hpl; rwa [allocP_lt hq] at this
275	    exact .frame hpl' (by simpa [allocEff, show ¬ s.P.length ≤ q by omega] using hd) ho hf
276	  | @place q o pl hpl hd ho _ ih =>
277	    have hpl' : s.P[q]? = some pl := by
278	      have : (allocP s ow ls)[q]? = some pl := hpl; rwa [allocP_lt hq] at this
279	    exact .place hpl' (by simpa [allocEff, show ¬ s.P.length ≤ q by omega] using hd) ho
280	      (ih (hw.owners.2.1 q pl o hpl' ho))
281	
282	/-- Every new place is usable when `owner` is (§40, §71.3, §71 `ok`). -/
283	theorem usable_new (hu : s.Usable ow) {q : Nat} (hq : s.P.length ≤ q)
284	    (hq' : q < s.P.length + ls.length) : (allocEff s ow ls).Usable q := by
285	  obtain ⟨i, rfl⟩ : ∃ i, q = s.P.length + i := ⟨q - s.P.length, by omega⟩
286	  exact .place (show (allocP s ow ls)[_]? = _ from allocP_new (by omega)) (by simp [allocEff]) rfl
287	    (usable_old hu)
288	
289	/-- `alloc` keeps the frame of the former places (§40, `placeFrame`; §49.3). -/
290	theorem frameOf_old (hw : WF3 s) {q f : Nat} (hq : q < s.P.length) :
291	    FrameOf (allocEff s ow ls) q f ↔ FrameOf s q f := by
292	  constructor
293	  · intro h
294	    induction h with
295	    | @frame q f pl hpl ho =>
296	      exact .frame (by have : (allocP s ow ls)[q]? = some pl := hpl; rwa [allocP_lt hq] at this) ho
297	    | @place q o f pl hpl ho _ ih =>
298	      have hpl' : s.P[q]? = some pl := by
299	        have : (allocP s ow ls)[q]? = some pl := hpl; rwa [allocP_lt hq] at this
300	      exact .place hpl' ho (ih (hw.owners.2.1 q pl o hpl' ho))
301	  · intro h
302	    clear hq
303	    induction h with
304	    | frame hpl ho =>
305	      exact .frame (show (allocP s ow ls)[_]? = _ by rw [allocP_lt (lt_of_getElem? hpl)]; exact hpl)
306	        ho
307	    | place hpl ho _ ih =>
308	      exact .place (show (allocP s ow ls)[_]? = _ by rw [allocP_lt (lt_of_getElem? hpl)]; exact hpl)
309	        ho ih
310	
311	/-- `alloc` keeps `placeFrame` of the former places (§40, §44). -/
312	theorem pframe_old (hw : WF3 s) {q : Nat} (hq : q < s.P.length) :
313	    (allocEff s ow ls).pframe q = s.pframe q :=
314	  Option.ext fun f => by rw [pframe_iff, pframe_iff, frameOf_old hw hq]
315	
316	end Usable
317	
318	/-! ## Effective anchors (§44) -/
319	
320	/-- A frame of the stack is its own ancestor (§39, `ancestor`). -/
321	theorem ancestor_self {f : Nat} : ∀ {F : Frames}, f ∈ F → ancestor F f f
322	  | g :: F, h => by
323	    unfold ancestor
324	    simp only [List.dropWhile_cons]
325	    by_cases e : g = f
326	    · subst e; simp
327	    · have hgf : (g != f) = true := by simp [e]
328	      simp only [hgf, ↓reduceIte]
329	      exact ancestor_self (List.mem_cons.1 h |>.resolve_left (fun h' => e h'.symm))

334	/-- The anchor-order condition of an existing authority carries over `alloc` (§44, §71 `ok`):
335	effective anchors, their holders and the frames of the former places are unchanged. -/
336	theorem effAnchorOK_old (hst : AllocStatic k s pr ow ls) (hw : WF3 s) {x : Nat}
337	    {fd : Option Nat} (h : EffAnchorOK s x fd) : EffAnchorOK (allocEff s ow ls) x fd := by
338	  have he : (allocEff s ow ls).effAnchor x = s.effAnchor x := by
339	    simp only [S3.effAnchor, ancs_eq hst]
340	  unfold EffAnchorOK at h ⊢
341	  rw [he]
342	  cases hz : s.A[s.effAnchor x]? with
343	  | none => rw [hz] at h; exact h.elim
344	  | some z =>
345	    rw [hz] at h
346	    rw [A_lt (lt_of_getElem? hz), hz]
347	    have hh : (allocEff s ow ls).hframe z.holder = s.hframe z.holder := by
348	      cases hzh : z.holder with
349	      | frame f => rfl
350	      | place p =>
351	        show (allocEff s ow ls).pframe p = s.pframe p
352	        cases hg : s.pframe p with
353	        | none => simp only [OptP, hzh, S3.hframe, hg] at h
354	        | some g => rw [← hg]; exact pframe_old hw (pframe_iff.1 hg).lt
355	    simp only [OptP] at h ⊢
356	    rw [hh]
357	    exact h
358	
359	/-- The new root authority satisfies the anchor-order condition for its holder `owner` (§44,
360	§71 `ok`): it is its own effective anchor, held by `owner`, whose frame is on the stack. -/
361	theorem effAnchorOK_new (hst : AllocStatic k s pr ow ls) :
362	    EffAnchorOK (allocEff s ow ls) s.A.length ((allocEff s ow ls).pframe ow) := by
363	  have hA : (allocEff s ow ls).A[s.A.length]? =
364	      some ⟨.modify, none, footprint (allocP s ow ls) s.P.length, .place ow, true⟩ := by
365	    rw [allocEff_A hst]; simp
366	  have he : (allocEff s ow ls).effAnchor s.A.length = s.A.length := by
367	    simp only [S3.effAnchor, S3.ancs,
368	      chain_none (show (allocEff s ow ls).org s.A.length = none by simp [S3.org, hA]),
369	      List.getLastD_nil]
370	  obtain ⟨f, hf, hfF⟩ := (usable_old (ls := ls) hst.ownerUsable).frameOf
371	  have hpf := pframe_iff.2 hf
372	  unfold EffAnchorOK
373	  rw [he, hA, hpf]
374	  simp only [OptP, S3.hframe, hpf]
375	  exact ancestor_self hfF
376	
377	end Anchor

382	variable {k : K} {s : S3} {pr ow : Nat} {ls : LocalShape}

384	/-- `alloc` preserves `RootChain` (§49.6, §71 `ok`): former authorities keep their chains and the
385	footprints of former places are unchanged; the new root authority is the root authority of the
386	new root place. -/
387	theorem rootChain (hst : AllocStatic k s pr ow ls) (hw : WF3 s) :
388	    RootChain (allocEff s ow ls) := by
389	  intro a y l ha hl hleaf
390	  rcases allocA_get hst ha with ⟨ha', hy⟩ | ⟨rfl, rfl⟩
391	  · obtain ⟨hlt, -⟩ := hw.footprints a y hy l hl
392	    obtain ⟨x0, z, r, hx0, hz, hzo, ⟨hrl, hrp⟩, hlr, hfz⟩ :=
393	      hw.rootChain a y l hy hl ((isLeaf_old hst.shapeOK hlt).1 hleaf)
394	    have hx0lt : x0 < s.A.length := by
395	      rcases hx0 with rfl | hx0
396	      · exact ha'
397	      · exact Nat.lt_trans (chain_lt hx0) ha'
398	    refine ⟨x0, z, r, by rw [ancs_eq hst]; exact hx0, by rw [A_lt hx0lt]; exact hz, hzo,
399	      ⟨by show r < (allocP s ow ls).length; rw [allocP_len]; omega,
400	       by show parentOf (allocP s ow ls) r = none; rw [parentOf_lt hrl]; exact hrp⟩,
401	      (partOf_old hlt).2 hlr, fun l' => ?_⟩
402	    show _ ↔ l' ∈ footprint (allocP s ow ls) r
403	    rw [footprint_old hst.shapeOK hrl]; exact hfz l'
404	  · exact ⟨s.A.length, _, s.P.length, .inl rfl, ha, rfl, root_new hst, (mem_footprint.1 hl).2.2,
405	      fun _ => Iff.rfl⟩
406	
407	/-- `alloc` preserves `RootHeld` (§49.7, §71 `ok`): former usable root places keep their root
408	authority; the new root place has the new root authority, held by its owner `owner`. -/
409	theorem rootHeld (hst : AllocStatic k s pr ow ls) (hw : WF3 s) :
410	    RootHeld (allocEff s ow ls) := by
411	  intro r hr hu
412	  by_cases hrl : r < s.P.length
413	  · have hr0 : RootPlace s.P r :=
414	      ⟨hrl, by rw [← parentOf_lt (ow := ow) (ls := ls) hrl]; exact hr.2⟩
415	    obtain ⟨i, z, pr', hz, za, zo, zm, hpr, hh, hf⟩ := hw.rootHeld r hr0 (usable_back hw hu hrl)
416	    exact ⟨i, z, pr', by rw [A_lt (lt_of_getElem? hz)]; exact hz, za, zo, zm,
417	      by show (allocP s ow ls)[r]? = _; rw [allocP_lt hrl]; exact hpr, hh,
418	      fun l => by
419	        show _ ↔ l ∈ footprint (allocP s ow ls) r
420	        rw [footprint_old hst.shapeOK hrl]; exact hf l⟩
421	  · obtain rfl := root_unique_new hst (by omega) hr
422	    exact ⟨s.A.length, ⟨.modify, none, footprint (allocP s ow ls) s.P.length, .place ow, true⟩, _,
423	      by rw [allocEff_A hst]; simp, rfl, rfl, rfl, allocP_root hst, rfl, fun _ => Iff.rfl⟩
424	
425	/-- `alloc` preserves `WF3` (§49, §71.3 "new identities and ownership relations must respect
426	`WF3`, `RootHeld`"). -/
427	theorem wf3 (hst : AllocStatic k s pr ow ls) (hw : WF3 s) : WF3 (allocEff s ow ls) where
428	  frames := hw.frames
429	  places q pl r hq hp := by
430	    rcases allocP_get hq with ⟨hql, hq'⟩ | ⟨hqn, -, -, how⟩
431	    · obtain ⟨pr', hpr, hlt, ho, hd⟩ := hw.places q pl r hq' hp
432	      refine ⟨pr', by show (allocP s ow ls)[r]? = _; rw [allocP_lt (by omega)]; exact hpr, hlt,
433	        ho, ?_⟩
434	      simp [allocEff, show ¬ s.P.length ≤ r by omega, show ¬ s.P.length ≤ q by omega, hd]
435	    · have hpo : parentOf (allocP s ow ls) q = some r := by
436	        simp only [parentOf]; rw [show (allocP s ow ls)[q]? = some pl from hq]; exact hp
437	      obtain ⟨hr, hrq⟩ := parentOf_ge hst.shapeOK hqn hpo
438	      have hrl : q < s.P.length + ls.length := by
439	        have := lt_of_getElem? hq; rwa [show (allocEff s ow ls).P = allocP s ow ls from rfl,
440	          allocP_len] at this
441	      obtain ⟨i, rfl⟩ : ∃ i, r = s.P.length + i := ⟨r - s.P.length, by omega⟩
442	      exact ⟨_, allocP_new (by omega), hrq, by rw [how],
443	        by simp [allocEff, hqn]⟩
444	  owners := ⟨fun q pl f hq ho => (by
445	      rcases allocP_get hq with ⟨-, hq'⟩ | ⟨-, -, -, how⟩
446	      · exact hw.owners.1 q pl f hq' ho
447	      · rw [how] at ho; cases ho),
448	    fun q pl o hq ho => (by
449	      show o < (allocP s ow ls).length
450	      rw [allocP_len]
451	      rcases allocP_get hq with ⟨-, hq'⟩ | ⟨-, -, -, how⟩
452	      · have := hw.owners.2.1 q pl o hq' ho; omega
453	      · rw [how] at ho; cases ho; have := hst.ownerUsable.lt; omega),
454	    fun _ hq => S3.Usable.frameOf hq⟩
455	  footprints a x hx l hl := by
456	    rcases allocA_get hst hx with ⟨-, hx'⟩ | ⟨-, rfl⟩
457	    · obtain ⟨hlt, hleaf⟩ := hw.footprints a x hx' l hl
458	      exact ⟨by show l < (allocP s ow ls).length; rw [allocP_len]; omega,
459	        (isLeaf_old hst.shapeOK hlt).2 hleaf⟩
460	    · obtain ⟨h1, h2, -⟩ := mem_footprint.1 hl
461	      exact ⟨h1, h2⟩
462	  origins b y a hb ho := by
463	    rcases allocA_get hst hb with ⟨-, hb'⟩ | ⟨-, rfl⟩
464	    · exact hw.origins b y a hb' ho
465	    · cases ho
466	  rootChain := rootChain hst hw
467	  rootHeld := rootHeld hst hw
468	  holders a y hy ya := by
469	    rcases allocA_get hst hy with ⟨-, hy'⟩ | ⟨-, rfl⟩
470	    · have := hw.holders a y hy' ya
471	      cases hh : y.holder with
472	      | frame f => rw [hh] at this; exact this
473	      | place p => rw [hh] at this; exact usable_old this
474	    · exact usable_old hst.ownerUsable
475	
476	/-- `alloc` preserves `I1` (§50, §71 `ok`): the new root authority covers only new leaves. -/
477	theorem i1 (hst : AllocStatic k s pr ow ls) (hw : WF3 s) (h1 : I1 s) :
478	    I1 (allocEff s ow ls) := by
479	  intro a b x y p hab ha hb xa ya xp yp hnab hnba
480	  rcases allocA_get hst ha with ⟨-, hx⟩ | ⟨rfl, rfl⟩ <;>
481	    rcases allocA_get hst hb with ⟨-, hy⟩ | ⟨rfl, rfl⟩
482	  · rw [ancs_eq hst] at hnab hnba
483	    exact h1 a b x y p hab hx hy xa ya xp yp hnab hnba
484	  · have := (hw.footprints a x hx p xp).1
485	    have := fp_new_ge (s := s) (ow := ow) (ls := ls) yp; omega
486	  · have := (hw.footprints b y hy p yp).1
487	    have := fp_new_ge (s := s) (ow := ow) (ls := ls) xp; omega
488	  · exact absurd rfl hab

490	/-- `alloc` preserves `I2` (§51, §71 `ok`): the new authority has no origin. -/
491	theorem i2 (hst : AllocStatic k s pr ow ls) (h2 : I2 s) : I2 (allocEff s ow ls) := by
492	  intro b y a hb ho
493	  rcases allocA_get hst hb with ⟨-, hb'⟩ | ⟨-, rfl⟩
494	  · obtain ⟨x₁, hx₁, hh⟩ := h2 b y a hb' ho
495	    exact ⟨x₁, by rw [A_lt (lt_of_getElem? hx₁)]; exact hx₁, hh⟩
496	  · cases ho

498	/-- `alloc` preserves `I3` (§52, §71 `ok`): the new places have no anchor. -/
499	theorem i3 (hw : WF3 s) (h3 : I3 s) : I3 (allocEff s ow ls) := by
500	  intro q hq x hx
501	  by_cases hql : q < s.P.length
502	  · have hx' : x ∈ s.D q := by simpa [allocEff, show ¬ s.P.length ≤ q by omega] using hx
503	    obtain ⟨y, hy, ya⟩ := h3 q (usable_back hw hq hql) x hx'
504	    exact ⟨y, by rw [A_lt (lt_of_getElem? hy)]; exact hy, ya⟩
505	  · simp [allocEff, show s.P.length ≤ q by omega] at hx

507	/-- `alloc` preserves `AnchorOrder` (§44, §54, §71 `ok`): the new places have no anchor and the
508	frames of the former places do not change. -/
509	theorem anchorOrder (hst : AllocStatic k s pr ow ls) (hw : WF3 s) (hao : AnchorOrder s) :
510	    AnchorOrder (allocEff s ow ls) := by
511	  intro q hq x hx
512	  by_cases hql : q < s.P.length
513	  · have hx' : x ∈ s.D q := by simpa [allocEff, show ¬ s.P.length ≤ q by omega] using hx
514	    rw [pframe_old hw hql]
515	    exact effAnchorOK_old hst hw (hao q (usable_back hw hq hql) x hx')
516	  · simp [allocEff, show s.P.length ≤ q by omega] at hx

518	/-- `alloc` preserves `NoDangling` (§54, §71 `ok`): former places keep their footprints and
519	usability; the new root authority covers only new places, which are usable. -/
520	theorem noDangling (hst : AllocStatic k s pr ow ls) (hw : WF3 s) (hnd : NoDangling s) :
521	    NoDangling (allocEff s ow ls) := by
522	  intro j z hz za q hq l hl hlz
523	  obtain ⟨hlP, -, hlq⟩ := mem_footprint.1 hl
524	  have hql : q ≤ l := by
525	    rcases hlq.2 with rfl | hc
526	    · exact Nat.le_refl _
527	    · exact Nat.le_of_lt (chain_lt hc)
528	  rcases allocA_get hst hz with ⟨-, hy⟩ | ⟨-, rfl⟩
529	  · have hlo := (hw.footprints j z hy l hlz).1
530	    have hqo : q < s.P.length := by omega
531	    exact hnd j z hy za q (fun hu => hq (usable_old hu)) l
532	      ((footprint_old hst.shapeOK hqo l).1 hl) hlz
533	  · have hge := fp_new_ge (s := s) (ow := ow) (ls := ls) hlz
534	    by_cases hqo : q < s.P.length
535	    · have := (mem_footprint.1 ((footprint_old hst.shapeOK hqo l).1 hl)).1; omega
536	    · have hlP' : l < (allocP s ow ls).length := hlP
537	      rw [allocP_len] at hlP'
538	      exact hq (usable_new hst.ownerUsable (by omega) (by omega))

540	/-- `alloc` preserves `AnchorOrderHeld` (§44, §54, §71 `ok`): former held authorities keep their
541	condition; the new root authority is its own effective anchor, held by `owner`. -/
542	theorem anchorOrderHeld (hst : AllocStatic k s pr ow ls) (hw : WF3 s) (h : AnchorOrderHeld s) :
543	    AnchorOrderHeld (allocEff s ow ls) := by
544	  intro q hq x y hx ya hh
545	  rcases allocA_get hst hx with ⟨-, hx'⟩ | ⟨rfl, rfl⟩
546	  · have hq0 : s.Usable q := by have := hw.holders x y hx' ya; rw [hh] at this; exact this
547	    rw [pframe_old hw hq0.lt]
548	    exact effAnchorOK_old hst hw (h q hq0 x y hx' ya hh)
549	  · cases hh
550	    exact effAnchorOK_new hst

554	theorem rootHeldConv (hst : AllocStatic k s pr ow ls) (hw : WF3 s) (hc : RootHeldConv s) :

556	  intro x z l r hx ho hl hr hlr
557	  rcases allocA_get hst hx with ⟨-, hx'⟩ | ⟨rfl, rfl⟩
558	  · have hlt := (hw.footprints x z hx' l hl).1
559	    have hlr' := (partOf_old hlt).1 hlr
560	    have hrl : r < s.P.length := by
561	      rcases hlr'.2 with rfl | hc'
562	      · exact hlt
563	      · exact Nat.lt_trans (chain_lt hc') hlt
564	    have hr' : RootPlace s.P r :=
565	      ⟨hrl, by rw [← parentOf_lt (ow := ow) (ls := ls) hrl]; exact hr.2⟩
566	    obtain ⟨pr', hpr, hh⟩ := hc x z l r hx' ho hl hr' hlr'
567	    exact ⟨pr', by show (allocP s ow ls)[r]? = _; rw [allocP_lt hrl]; exact hpr, hh⟩
568	  · obtain rfl := rootOf_unique hr (root_new hst) hlr (mem_footprint.1 hl).2.2
569	    exact ⟨_, allocP_root hst, rfl⟩

579	/-! ## Main results (§57, §58, §71) -/
580	
581	/-- `alloc` preserves the main invariant (§57, §58: an `ok` transition preserves the invariants;
582	§71.3: the new identities and ownership relations respect `WF3` and `RootHeld`): from a state
583	satisfying `KInv`, the `ok` outcome of `alloc` satisfies `KInv`. -/
584	theorem alloc_preserves {k : K} {pr ow : Nat} {ls : LocalShape} {s s' : S3}
585	    (hk : KInv s) (h : AllocStep k pr ow ls s (.ok s')) : KInv s' := by
586	  cases h with
587	  | ok hst _ =>
588	    obtain ⟨hw, ⟨⟨h1, h2, h3, -⟩, hao, hnd⟩, haoh, -⟩ := hk
589	    exact kInv_of (Alloc.wf3 hst hw)
590	        ⟨⟨Alloc.i1 hst hw h1, Alloc.i2 hst h2, Alloc.i3 hw h3, i4_always _⟩,
591	          Alloc.anchorOrder hst hw hao, Alloc.noDangling hst hw hnd⟩
592	        (Alloc.anchorOrderHeld hst hw haoh)

594	/-- `alloc` preserves the auxiliary `KAux` (`RootHeldConv`, §40, §49.7; §71 `ok`) from a `KInv`
595	state. -/
596	theorem alloc_preserves_kAux {k : K} {pr ow : Nat} {ls : LocalShape} {s s' : S3}
597	    (hk : KInv s) (ha : KAux s) (h : AllocStep k pr ow ls s (.ok s')) : KAux s' := by
598	  cases h with
599	  | ok hst _ => exact Alloc.rootHeldConv hst hk.1 ha

601	/-- The `ok` effect of `alloc` (§71, `ok`): the former places are kept and the nonempty shape is
602	appended with fresh identities, every new place owned by `owner`; among the new places exactly
603	one, `|P|`, is a root place (a new storage root); exactly one authority is added, at the fresh
604	identity `|A|`: the root `Modify` authority of `|P|`, with no origin, held by `owner`, covering
605	the footprint of `|P|`; the leaves of `|P|` are `Uninit`. -/
606	theorem alloc_one_root {k : K} {pr ow : Nat} {ls : LocalShape} {s s' : S3}
607	    (h : AllocStep k pr ow ls s (.ok s')) :
608	    s'.P.length = s.P.length + ls.length ∧ 0 < ls.length ∧
609	    (∀ q < s.P.length, s'.P[q]? = s.P[q]?) ∧
610	    (∀ (q : Nat) (pl : Place), s.P.length ≤ q → s'.P[q]? = some pl → pl.owner = .place ow) ∧
611	    RootPlace s'.P s.P.length ∧
612	    (∀ r, s.P.length ≤ r → RootPlace s'.P r → r = s.P.length) ∧
613	    s'.A = s.A ++ [⟨.modify, none, footprint s'.P s.P.length, .place ow, true⟩] ∧
614	    ∀ l ∈ footprint s'.P s.P.length, s'.I l = .uninit := by
615	  cases h with
616	  | ok hst _ =>
617	    refine ⟨Alloc.allocP_len s ow ls, Alloc.len_pos hst, fun q hq => Alloc.allocP_lt hq,
618	      fun q pl hq hpl => ?_, Alloc.root_new hst,
619	      fun r hr hrp => Alloc.root_unique_new hst hr hrp, Alloc.allocEff_A hst, fun l hl => ?_⟩
620	    · rcases Alloc.allocP_get hpl with ⟨hq', -⟩ | ⟨-, -, -, how⟩
621	      · omega
622	      · exact how
623	    · have := Alloc.fp_new_ge (s := s) (ow := ow) (ls := ls) hl
624	      simp [allocEff, this]
625	
626	/-- `alloc` is deterministic (§58, §71): its outcome is a function of the state and the
627	arguments. -/
628	theorem alloc_det {k : K} {pr ow : Nat} {ls : LocalShape} {s : S3} {o₁ o₂ : Outcome3 S3}
629	    (h₁ : AllocStep k pr ow ls s o₁) (h₂ : AllocStep k pr ow ls s o₂) : o₁ = o₂ := by
630	  cases h₁ <;> cases h₂ <;> first | rfl | contradiction

632	/-- A failed `alloc` leaves the state unchanged (§58: `fail` is a defined failure leaving the
633	state unchanged; §71: `fail` when the static preconditions hold but `K.Satisfiable` is false, no
634	state change). The `fail` outcome carries no state, so the state stays `s`; moreover the failure
635	happens only when the static preconditions hold and `K.Satisfiable(provider, shape, s)` is false,
636	and then no `ok` successor state exists. -/
637	theorem alloc_fail_unchanged {k : K} {pr ow : Nat} {ls : LocalShape} {s : S3}
638	    (h : AllocStep k pr ow ls s .fail) :
639	    AllocStatic k s pr ow ls ∧ ¬ k.Satisfiable pr ls s ∧
640	      ∀ s', ¬ AllocStep k pr ow ls s (.ok s') := by
641	  cases h with
642	  | fail h1 h2 => exact ⟨h1, h2, fun _ h' => by cases alloc_det (.fail h1 h2) h'⟩
643

645	`ok` or `reject`"): none of the other fifteen operation relations of `KStep` yields `fail`. -/
646	theorem fail_only_alloc (k : K) (s : S3) :
647	    (∀ src region m, ¬ DeriveStep src region m s .fail) ∧
648	    (∀ src rs, ¬ SplitStep k src rs s .fail) ∧
649	    (∀ a, ¬ ReleaseStep a s .fail) ∧

651	    (∀ q x, ¬ DependStep q x s .fail) ∧
652	    (∀ ps ls, ¬ EnterStep ps ls s .fail) ∧
653	    ¬ ExitStep k s .fail ∧

655	    (∀ a ls, ¬ Write3Step a ls s .fail) ∧
656	    (∀ a ls, ¬ WriteSharedStep k a ls s .fail) ∧
657	    (∀ p, ¬ PinStep p s .fail) ∧
658	    (∀ p, ¬ UnpinStep k p s .fail) ∧
659	    (∀ p, ¬ EndUseStep k p s .fail) ∧
660	    (∀ p auth, ¬ FreeStep k p auth s .fail) ∧
661	    (∀ a p, ¬ StoreStep a p s .fail) :=
662	  ⟨fun _ _ _ => Alloc.guarded_ne_fail, fun _ _ => Alloc.guarded_ne_fail,
663	    fun _ => Alloc.guarded_ne_fail, fun _ _ => Alloc.guarded_ne_fail,
664	    fun _ _ => Alloc.guarded_ne_fail, fun _ _ => Alloc.guarded_ne_fail, Alloc.guarded_ne_fail,
665	    fun _ _ => Alloc.guarded_ne_fail, fun _ _ => Alloc.guarded_ne_fail,

import Ern.MemoryModel.Access.Lemmas

/-!
# Access kernel: the preserved invariant

The conjunction that every kernel step must preserve (§57 of
`specs/ERN_Memory_Model_Specification_v0.1.md`) and the auxiliary invariant carried with it. The per-operation preservation modules state their results with these two predicates.
-/

namespace Ern.MemoryModel.Access

/-- The kernel invariant of §57: `WF3 ∧ Inv3 ∧ AnchorOrderHeld ∧ NoOrphan`. -/
def KInv (s : S3) : Prop := WF3 s ∧ Inv3 s ∧ AnchorOrderHeld s ∧ NoOrphan s

/-- Auxiliary invariant carried with `KInv`, not a clause of §57 (§40, §49.7): the converse
root-holder property `RootHeldConv`, which is not a clause of `WF3`. -/
def KAux (s : S3) : Prop := RootHeldConv s

/-- `NoOrphan` follows from `WF3` (§54, §49.7), so `KInv` reduces to its first three
conjuncts. -/
theorem kInv_of {s : S3} (hw : WF3 s) (hi : Inv3 s) (ha : AnchorOrderHeld s) : KInv s :=
  ⟨hw, hi, ha, noOrphan_of_wf3 hw⟩

end Ern.MemoryModel.Access
